smells.finding: New/changed functions are all short: _artifact_match_satisfied (~4 lines body), _fault_artifact_malformed_match_list (~20 lines, one loop with two early-continue branches), the inline non-dict-match guards at both call sites (1 isinstance check each). No method grew unreasonably.
No class gained responsibilities beyond one new attribute (ValidationResult.report_only) and its constructor/str wiring; ValidationResult stays a thin list subclass.
The diff actively REMOVES pre-existing duplication: _check_condition's and attest's near-identical match-comparison expressions are now both delegated to one shared _artifact_match_satisfied helper.
No method reaches into another object's internals more than its own; the new helper operates on plain dicts passed in directly.
No repeated group of parameters travels together across signatures; payload/match stay as single dict arguments.

Fault codes remain plain strings, consistent with the pre-existing Fault dataclass's own convention (code: str) used throughout validate_spine.py before this diff -- not a new primitive obsession introduced here.
_artifact_match_satisfied(payload, want) and _fault_artifact_malformed_match_list(where, check) both take 2 parameters.

One conceptual change (widen the match comparator + add a matching validate_spine shape/falsifiability fault) touches checklist_engine.py at 2 call sites plus validate_spine.py's fault family -- that is the change's natural footprint, not scattered incidental edits.

checklist_engine.py and validate_spine.py each changed for exactly one reason (the match-shape widening and its corresponding shape/falsifiability faults respectively); no unrelated reason for change was mixed in.
No new chained accessor calls; chk.get("match", {}) and payload.get(k) are single-hop lookups, unchanged in shape from the pre-existing code.

_JSON_SCALAR_TYPES and the malformed-list check exist only to serve decision:malformed-list-definition, which the handoff names explicitly -- no unused hook or generalized-for-the-future abstraction was added.

The new comments (decision: pointers, the promotion-trigger block, the bool/int JSON-scalar note) explain non-obvious WHY -- a graded decision, a subtle invariant (isinstance(True, int)), a promotion rule -- not WHAT; the code itself (short, well-named helpers) does not need the comments to be understood. This matches the repo's existing convention of inline `# decision:<id>` comments beside code implementing a graded decision (2 pre-existing instances already in scripts/gauge_reader.py before this diff), so the comment density is not compensating for unclear structure.
